events.continuity_hook: Keep the booked outbound and hotel, the accepted later return flight, seats for all three travelers, post-checkout luggage arrangement, final airport departure timing, and any airline schedule-change notation together as the completed weekend itinerary.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm that retaining the rescheduled flight requires no action or added payment and record the final Monday luggage and airport timeline.
events.scenario_brief: The earlier Monday flight now has only scattered seats and requires an additional payment for all three travelers, while the rescheduled booked flight still has their seats together. The hotel will store their bags after checkout, and a late lunch near the museum district would fill most of the added wait without changing airport transportation.

events.continuity_hook: Carry the viable Sunday-evening and Monday-morning arrivals, Nashville meeting time, drive estimate to Memphis, two Tuesday return options, and airfare totals into the lodging and car search.
events.interaction_goal: Compare round-trip and open-jaw flight structures against both work appointments and choose the schedule to price as a complete trip.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus must attend a Monday morning regional meeting in Nashville and inspect a Memphis restaurant Tuesday afternoon. A Chicago-Nashville round trip would require a long return drive after the inspection, while flying into Nashville and home from Memphis adds airfare but shortens Tuesday evening; the earliest Monday arrival leaves little margin before the meeting.

events.continuity_hook: Retain the selected open-jaw flights, two hotel pairs, complete one-way car pricing, drop charge, pickup and return hours, Monday Nashville-to-Memphis drive, and Tuesday hotel-to-inspection and inspection-to-airport times.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the full cost and timing of the hotel-and-car combinations, confirm that the Tuesday sequence reaches the airport on time, and select one combination without purchasing.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus has selected a Sunday-evening flight to Nashville and a Tuesday-evening return from Memphis. He needs one night near the Nashville meeting, one night near the Memphis restaurant, and a one-way car; the least expensive rental quote excludes the intercity drop charge, and one Memphis hotel would force a cross-town drive during the Tuesday afternoon window.

events.continuity_hook: Keep the completed flight, two hotel, and rental confirmations with final totals, cancellation deadlines, included one-way charge, counter hours, Monday intercity route, and Tuesday inspection-to-airport schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Recheck dates, traveler details, totals, and car-return timing, then book all components if nothing has materially changed.
events.scenario_brief: Both selected hotels remain available at cancellable one-night rates, and the rental company has confirmed that the displayed total includes the one-way charge. The Tuesday return flight has risen slightly but still leaves adequate time after the inspection when the car is returned at the Memphis airport counter.

events.continuity_hook: Carry the three-passenger totals for the Saturday and Friday outbound choices, Thursday and Friday return choices, flight times, added-night implication, and usable vacation time into the neighborhood and hotel comparison.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the four practical flight combinations including any added lodging night, and choose dates for the hotel search without buying tickets.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus and his family are considering six nights in San Diego during their son's school break, with fixed availability from Saturday through the following Friday. Nonstop flights for three are costly on Saturday, while leaving Friday evening lowers the fare but creates a seventh hotel night; returning Thursday evening is cheaper but removes their planned final beach day.

events.continuity_hook: Retain both lodging candidates, room layouts for three travelers, full taxes and nightly charges, breakfast terms, parking costs, cancellation dates, beach access, and estimated travel times to the zoo, airport, and planned waterfront activities.
events.interaction_goal: Verify sleeping arrangements and three-person occupancy, compare complete six-night costs and local travel implications, and narrow the lodging choice without reserving it.
events.scenario_brief: The family has narrowed the trip to a Saturday-through-Friday flight schedule and is comparing six-night stays in Mission Bay and Coronado. The Mission Bay room has two queens and a lower base price but adds nightly parking and a resort charge; the Coronado suite has a king and sofa bed, includes breakfast, and requires confirmation that the sofa bed and quoted occupancy cover their 12-year-old.
